newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - July 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Three major parties try to mobilise members for National Assembly vote to decide on constitutional reforms.
Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen says will consider setting up representatitive office in Taiwan.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - Ruling Nationalist Party considers including plebiscite as part of constitutional reforms.
Hun Sen says hopes to establish direct links with Taiwan.
LIBERTY TIMES - Five dead, nine injured in southern Pingtung car accident.
Thousands take to streets of Taipei demanding right to hold plebiscites.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Government has no immediate plans to adjust basic wages for public workers.
Editorial - Only stable stock market can protect investors' interests.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Central bank's recent liquidity mop-ups light in value, but high in frequency.
Many Taiwan investors still sanguine about business opportunities in Cambodia despite recent violence there.
